name: Indus Towers
step12_scaling_decision: A five-year projection of the credit path WAS built (Companies/indus-towers/forward_model.py), with base and stress cases and the funding path DERIVED rather than assumed (failure mode 18). What was NOT run is the equity-research plugin's native 3-statement workbook. Reason: a generic 3-statement template models revenue as a growth percentage, and for a tower company that is the wrong primitive. Revenue is co-locations multiplied by revenue per co-location, and the TENANCY RATIO - the metric this sector lives by - has to fall out of the tower and co-location paths rather than being assumed alongside them. The model is built that way, which is what made the two-year tenancy DECLINE (1.677 to 1.626 to 1.618) a modelled variable instead of a footnote, and what let the stress case flex it directly to 1.366. It also tracks borrowings and lease liabilities separately, which is not optional on this issuer: at FY2026 borrowings were Rs 920.9 crore against Rs 20,206.0 crore of ground leases, so a single 'total debt' line would misdescribe the balance sheet. Earnings are normalised throughout for the Vodafone Idea provision write-backs (Rs 5,077.1 crore FY2025, Rs 256.0 crore FY2026), without which FY2026 EBITDA reads as a 12.9% FALL when underlying EBITDA GREW 12.9%. Twelve opening-balance tie-outs. Recorded 01-Sep-2026.
